# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 14 NOVEMBER DAYS

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

The brilliant hues that had shone for weeks beside the margins of Seven Gulls Harbor had dissolved into the muted gray-blue of late autumn hills. Numerous days arrived in which mist-laden rain obscured the fields and shores, or where they trembled in the chill of a doleful wind from the sea—as well as nights filled with storm and tempest, during which Nell would occasionally wake to offer prayers that no vessel was striving along the formidable north coast, because under such conditions not even the immense, steadfast beacon revolving fearlessly amid the dark could succeed in steering it to a secure refuge.
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0000 }

“In November I sometimes feel as if spring could never come again,” she sighed, lamenting the utter ugliness of her frozen and messily ruined flower-plots. The cheerful small garden of the schoolmaster’s bride was a somewhat dismal spot at present, and the Lombardies and birches were under bare poles, in the words of Captain Saul. Yet the fir-forest in back of the small house remained perpetually green and steadfast; and even during November and December gentle days occurred featuring sunlight and violet hazes, when the harbor leaped and gleamed as cheerfully as in the middle of summer, and the gulf was so mildly blue and delicate that the tempest and the fierce wind appeared merely to be elements of a ancient dream.
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0001 }

Numerous autumn evenings were spent by Nell and Hugh at the lighthouse. A cheery place it remained at all times. Hints of sunshine appeared to be hiding everywhere around it, even on occasions when the sea was lifeless and gray while the east wind sang in a minor key. This was possibly due to the First Mate constantly strutting through it adorned in gold. The sun was scarcely missed because he was so big and radiant, and the laughter together with the conversation taking place beside Captain Saul’s fireplace was pleasantly accompanied by his booming purrs. On topics exceeding the understanding of cat or king, Captain Saul and Hugh engaged in numerous lengthy discussions and elevated discourse.
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0002 }

“I enjoy reflecting upon every type of issue, even if I am unable to resolve them,” Captain Saul stated. “It was my father's belief that we ought to refrain from discussing matters beyond our comprehension, yet if we followed that rule, doctor, our topics of discourse would be exceptionally scarce. I suppose the gods frequently chuckle upon listening to us, but it is of no consequence provided we keep in mind that we are merely human and refrain from imagining that we are actually divine entities ourselves, possessing knowledge of right and wrong. I suppose our discussions will not cause much injury to us or to anybody else, so let us attempt another go at the origin, purpose, and destination tonight, doctor.”
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0003 }

Nell either paid attention or drifted into thought as the others “whacked.” On occasion, Lorna accompanied them to the lighthouse, where she and Nell strolled the coast during the strange dusk, or remained perched on the boulders beneath the lighthouse structure until nightfall forced them to return to the cozy driftwood fire. At that point, Captain Saul would make tea for them and recount
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0004 }

“stories about the earth and ocean, and whatever could happen to the vast, overlooked realm beyond.”
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0005 }

Lorna appeared to forever take great pleasure in those lighthouse revelries, flowering for the duration into swift humor and lovely laughter, or silence with shining eyes. The discourse possessed a particular zest and flavor while Lorna was there that was absent during her nonattendance. She appeared to stimulate brilliance in everyone else even when she refrained from speaking. Captain Saul narrated his tales with greater skill, Hugh proved swifter in debate and quick retorts, and Nell sensed small spurts and streams of whim and creativity welling up to her lips beneath the sway of Lorna’s persona.
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0006 }

“Far removed from Seven Gulls, that girl came into the world destined to head intellectual and social spheres,” she remarked to Hugh while they strolled toward their house one evening. “Here she is simply wasted—wasted.”
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0007 }

“Didn’t you hear Captain Saul and me the other evening as we were talking about that matter in a general way? It was our reassuring deduction that the Creator likely understood how to manage His universe just as effectively as we do, and that, in the end, 'wasted’ lives do not exist, unless a person deliberately throws away and ruins his own life—a thing Lorna Vane definitely has not done. Furthermore, certain folks could consider that a Wexcombe B.A., who was starting to be recognized by editors, was 'wasted’ by becoming the spouse of a hardworking country doctor in the small town of Seven Gulls.”
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0008 }

“Hugh!”
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0009 }

“Now, had Cyril Lisle been the man you wed,” Hugh went on without pity, “'a leader in social and intellectual circles far away from Seven Gulls' is what YOU might have become.”
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0010 }

“Hugh CARROW!”
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0011 }

“You ARE aware that he had your affection once, Nell.”
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0012 }

“Hugh, that is cruel—'pisen mean, just as all the men are,’ to quote Miss Winifred. I was NEVER in love with him. It was merely my imagination. You are aware of that. You KNOW that I would prefer being your wife within our house of dreams and fulfillment to being a queen inside a palace.”
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0013 }

Hugh did not respond verbally; nevertheless, I fear they both failed to think of poor Lorna as she hurried alone through the fields toward a dwelling that was far from being a palace or the realization of a dream.
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0014 }

At their backs, the rising moon began to transform the dark, melancholy sea. Across the harbor, where her illumination had not yet arrived, the distant shoreline appeared shadowy and evocative, full of faint coves, deep darkness, and sparkling lights.
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0015 }

“In what way the home lights beam through the night!” exclaimed Nell. “The harbor’s line of them resembles a necklace. And see what a glitter shines up at the Glen! Oh, see, Hugh; ours is right there. Leaving it lit makes me so happy. Returning to a pitch-black home is something I detest. OUR homelight, Hugh! Is it not wonderful to behold?”
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0016 }

“Nell—girl—it is merely a single dwelling among the countless millions on earth, yet it is ours—OURS—our guiding light in 'a naughty world.’ Once a man possesses a home containing a beloved, tiny, red-haired wife, what additional thing could he possibly request from life?”
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0017 }

“Well, ONE additional request might come from him,” Nell softly murmured with joy. “Oh, Hugh, I feel as though waiting until springtime is simply IMPOSSIBLE for me.”
{: #nw-v04-c14-p0018 }
